findings.summary: Informational: the planner computes the desired publication fingerprint but the pipeline does not consume ArtworkRegenerationDecision.DesiredFingerprint; this is harmless because the renderer is the sole computer of the stored fingerprint from the same inputs.
findings.detail: ArtworkRegenerationPlanner.ComputeDesiredFingerprint uses the same RenderFingerprint.ComputeOutputFingerprint, BadgeDefinitionResolver.Resolve, source identity (PublishedArtworkState.SourceFingerprint plus SourceCaptureIdentity dimensions) and configuration/renderer/schema inputs that SkiaBadgeRenderer uses (src/ArrTags/Rendering/SkiaBadgeRenderer.cs:284-302). ArtworkPublishingWorkItemProcessor ignores decision.DesiredFingerprint and the publisher stores the renderer's actual RenderResult.OutputFingerprint (src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkPublisher.cs:290/486). Because the retained-source read resolves the same artifact hash and capture dimensions (ArtworkSourceAuditStore content addressing guarantees artifact.Info.Sha256 == SourceArtifactId == SourceFingerprint), the two values cannot diverge in production. No change required.

findings.summary: Informational: the artwork stage is best-effort after a successful metadata publication and is not retried inside the same work item; a transient render/publication failure is re-driven by the next event, schedule, or webhook.
findings.detail: ArtworkPublishingWorkItemProcessor returns the metadata reconciliation classification even when regeneration is blocked or fails (src/ArrTags/Updates/ArtworkPublishingWorkItemProcessor.cs:100-131), and the coordinator converts render/publication failures into bounded results that preserve the current artwork. The worker documented this deliberate behavior. It does not violate a task acceptance criterion: architecture section 9 step 11 requires a failed render/publication to leave the current usable artwork unchanged, which it does. No change required.

findings.summary: Informational: no live Jellyfin host is available, so host-guarded and native-Skia facts skip; however the task-owned config-to-render integration test does not skip and exercises the real coordinator/publisher with an injected fingerprinting renderer.
findings.detail: RendererConfigurationIntegrationTests.ResolvedConfigurationReachesTheRenderAndChangesTheOutput ran and passed on this Alpine/musl environment (independently reproduced: Passed 1, Skipped 0). It resolves an overridden palette and a disabled Quality selector through PluginConfigurationSnapshot/RendererConfigurationResolver, drives the real ArtworkGenerationCoordinator, and asserts the resolved definitions/policy reached the render request and that the committed PublishedFingerprint differs from the default-configuration fingerprint. The native Skia golden/behavior/determinism tests continue to skip as expected on musl; that is the disclosed environment limitation, not a voided finding. No change required.
